title: Onprem k8s health and upgrade cheatsheet
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, operationally-focused checklist + notes doc to validate on-prem Kubernetes clusters (bare metal and vSphere), capture Terraform module boundaries, and outline a low-risk rolling upgrade canary plan. It is intentionally terse — intended for on-call / field engineers doing pre-upgrade preflight and quick recovery steps.

Scope:
- Applies to on-prem clusters maintained by eng-private-deployments (VPC-style private control plane or air-gapped bare metal).
- Covers health checks, terraform drift detection, node/cni/gpu preflight, and a staged upgrade sequence for kube control plane and node pools.
- Does NOT replace full runbooks for disaster recovery; instead a fast checklist for 30–90 minute maintenance windows.

Quick preflight (30m):
1) Confirm state access and locking
   - terraform state: ensure backend reachable (minio/consul/s3).
   - Check state lock: terraform force-unlock only with approval.
   - Command examples: 
     - aws s3 ls s3://redwood-terraform-state/prod || echo "state unreachable"
     - consul kv get terraform/locks/cluster-prod

2) Control plane health (kube-apiserver, etcd)
   - kubectl get componentstatuses || curl -k https://127.0.0.1:6443/healthz
   - etcd: member list, db size, recent leader changes
   - etcdctl --endpoints=https://etcd0:2379 endpoint status --write-out=table

3) Node and networking checks
   - kubectl get nodes -o wide -> ensure Ready and kubelet versions consistent
   - CNI: list pods in kube-system (calico/cilium/antrea), check logs for flapping
   - Check MTU mismatches on bare metal L2 networks (common perf bug)

4) GPU and driver validation (if inference nodes present)
   - nvidia-smi on each GPU host, confirm driver version matches recommended kernel
   - kubectl describe ds nvidia-device-plugin -n kube-system -> check crashloop events

5) Workload smoke tests
   - Simple inference endpoint test: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer test" http://ingress.example.com/health | jq .status
   - Canary a small batch of requests to ensure model-container init + KV cache warmup behave

Terraform module notes (practical heuristics):
- Module boundaries we use in repo: cluster_network, control_plane, node_pools, storage, vsphere_provider, bootstrap_images. Keep these modules small and idempotent.
- State layout suggestion: one state per environment (prod/stage), split states for control_plane vs node_pools to allow independent refresh/apply for node scaling without touching control plane state.
- Locking: consul lock for terraform apply is preferred in on-prem. Fallback: object-store based locks with Dynamo-style lease if using S3-compatible store.
- Secrets: do NOT store cloud credentials in terraform state; use sealed-secrets or vault provider to inject at apply time.
- Provider pinning: lock vsphere and kube providers to minor versions in module root to avoid surprise diffs during upgrade.

Common terraform gotchas and fixes:
- vSphere provider schema changes -> terraform plan shows large diffs for NIC ordering. Mitigation: add lifecycle ignore_changes for nic ordering fields or adopt stable device naming in templates.
- Floating IP vs host_entry drift on baremetal -> scripts that manage DNS should be the source of truth; treat terraform-managed hostnames as non-authoritative if external CMDB updates occur.

Rolling upgrade plan (control plane + nodes) — low-risk canary approach (target downtime: none):
Phase A - Prep (T-1 to T-0):
- Notify stakeholders and create incident channel.
- Run preflight checklist above. Take etcd snapshot and copy to offsite: ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot save /tmp/etcd-snap-$(date +%F).db --endpoints=https://etcd0:2379 --cacert=...
- Export manifest of running critical workloads for quick reapply.

Phase B - Control plane canary (T+0):
- Upgrade one control-plane node only (if HA >=3). Sequence: drain worker node workloads referencing this control plane (if any), cordon, reboot/replace control plane VM/host.
- Verify etcd cluster healthy and apiserver metrics OK for 10–15 minutes.
- smoke: kubectl get --raw /readyz || curl -sSf https://127.0.0.1:6443/readyz

Phase C - Node pool canary (T+30):
- Choose one small node-pool (1–3 nodes) as canary. For each node: cordon -> drain (respect terminationGracePeriodSeconds) -> apply new kubelet + driver packages -> uncordon. Validate workloads land on target.
- Check GPU pods scheduling if applicable. Run inference load sim for 5–10 minutes.

Phase D - Batch rollout (if canary green)
- Roll remaining node pools in waves, 10–20% capacity at a time depending on cluster size.
- Monitor: pod evictions, pending pods, restart counts, API latency, etcd leader changes.

Phase E - Post-upgrade validation
- Run end-to-end smoke suite (ingress, model inference, KV cache hits).
- Check rollout metrics in console: token latency, tail latency P99, and cost-per-token changes (quick sanity).
- Save diagnostic artifacts: kube-apiserver logs, kubelet logs for nodes that failed, terraform plan output.

Rollback signals (abort and revert):
- New failures in >2 node pools or sustained API latency >500ms for 10m.
- Model inference error rate increase >3x baseline or error surge for core routes.
- Action: pause rollout, isolate canary node, and if control plane issue, roll back to previous kube-apiserver binary image and restore etcd snapshot if necessary.

Quick recovery snippets (commands):
- Drain a node safely: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
- Replace node from terraform: terraform apply -target=module.node_pools["gpu"].vsphere_compute
- Force-unlock terraform state (last resort): terraform force-unlock <LOCK_ID>
- Restore etcd snapshot (single node step): ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot restore /tmp/etcd-snap.db --data-dir /var/lib/etcd/newdata --initial-cluster ...

Tips and heuristics (ops knowledge):
- Always test terraform changes in a cloned stage cluster with identical provider versions.
- For vSphere, use custom images with cloud-init metadata baked in; avoid post-boot provisioning when possible.
- Prefer kubelet/containerd upgrades that are one minor version at a time; skipping minors invites CRI/kernel mismatches.
- Maintain a small set of golden images for GPU nodes pinned to a validated driver/CUDA combo.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Can we add an automated preflight job that runs nightly and posts a drift report to a Slack channel? (action: Aisha to prototype using terraform plan --detailed-exitcode)
- Decide whether to split terraform states by AZ/rack for very large clusters (pros: blast radius, cons: complexity).
- Document exact node pool sizing heuristics for inference-heavy workloads (gpu vs cpu-only).

Notes-to-self / quick links:
- Field checklist gist:  https://gist.github.com/diego/onprem-preflight (WIP)
- PR for provider pinning: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-deployments/pull/217
- Jira: PLA-482 tracks the upgrade automation pipeline

If you use this checklist in a maintenance window and hit a novel failure mode, paste the log snippet into this doc and add a short root-cause note so the next on-call doesn’t re-discover it.

END OF CHEATSHEET
